Tests pass and typecheck printed nothing (clean); lint couldn't run (tool missing).

Negative numbers in JS-object-style strings, such as `{a: -1}`, now parse correctly when `acceptJSObject` is set. The cause was that esprima parses `-1` as a `UnaryExpression`, and `syntaxNodeToValue` in `packages/workflow/src/utils.ts` had no case for it. It returned `undefined`.

I added a `UnaryExpression` case that handles `-` and `+` on numeric operands and returns `undefined` for anything else. I also added a test in `packages/workflow/test/utils.test.ts` covering negative numbers at top level, in arrays, in nested objects and as decimals.

`acdc-test` on `utils.test.ts` passed all 111 tests. `acdc-typecheck` printed nothing, which I took as clean. `acdc-lint` failed to run because the `oxlint-tsgolint` executable wasn't found, so the change is unlinted.
